method.hdbscan: Hard HDBSCAN labels from assignments_hdbscan.json; cluster_id=-1 is noise.
method.human_annotated_read: HDBSCAN core members kept on their labeled theme. Each cluster_id=-1 feature was coded by an LLM against the Stage-4 theme definitions (human-style thematic assignment), or marked other. Residual themes are optional groupings within leftover other features.

themes.cluster_label: Apply same moderation standard across both sides
themes.definition: Participants reported that seeing original-plus-mirror pairs helped them judge more consistently and fairly by applying identical moderation criteria regardless of political viewpoint.

example.feature_value: Seeing the posts side-by-side helps them avoid bias and focus on whether each enables healthy debate
example.evidence_span: Seeing both posts side-by-side puts the words into perspective... I was just trying to focus on the core of each post and whether or not it would provide a well-intentioned space for healthy debate or discussion.

example.feature_value: They look for substance for healthy conversation; profanity/rhetoric leads to rejection, and mirror-image reasoning suggests common ground.
example.evidence_span: I look for some substance that could spark healthy conversation... If the messages were mostly rhetoric or contained profanity, I rejected... how the reasoning could be created into "mirror images"... we should be able to find some common ground.

themes.definition: High-influence reflections describe using a high bar for moderation that generally keeps opinions but removes posts when they become threatening, excessively vulgar, slanderous, or otherwise toxic/inflammatory.

example.feature_value: Approved heated posts if respectful; removed posts with harmful language or unproductive conversation.
example.evidence_span: approving politically heated posts as long as they were remaining respectful... chose to remove posts that contained harmful language or just didn't promote productive conversation.

example.feature_value: Supports free speech generally but targeted ad hominem attacks at specific people for removal.
example.evidence_span: I'm a fan of free speech but I disagree with ad hominem... attacks where people say horrible things about a specific person... Only one pair of posts contained an ad hominem attack and that was the pair I indicated I would remove.

themes.definition: Participants endorse keeping most speech (including opposing opinions) while justifying removal only when content involves threats, intent to harm, or violence and sometimes closely related “bad language” or profanity.

example.feature_value: Default to free speech if no threats; removal only if threats/intent to harm are present
example.evidence_span: both sides deserve free speech... If someone mad threats... then that is different i think then they should be taken down but i didn't see any threats

example.feature_value: Typically keep; only remove for outrageously sensationalized, likely faked statistical claims or violent calls to action
example.evidence_span: none of the post pairs were nearly extreme or problematic enough to warrant removal except for the one outrageously sensationalized... violent calls to action are the only things

example.feature_value: Keep opinions; remove if nonsense/lies with harmful effects
example.evidence_span: If it was something that was mainly an opinion, I thought it should stay... If it appeared to be nonsense... and I thought it was actually harmful, I thought it should be removed... But if they are flat out lies, I think they should not remain.

residual_themes.theme_label: Pair-level “reasonableness” / argument quality as the keep-or-remove driver
residual_themes.definition: Across leftover items, decisions are guided by whether each paired post (and/or the pair together) is reasonable, coherent, substantive, and makes a real argument (vs nonsense, rambling, name-calling, trolling, or incoherence).

example.feature_value: Used a point-or-nonsense check; if arguments could be made, tended to allow
example.evidence_span: make sure that each post was making a point or was it nonsensical dribble... If you could argue for each point, I generally decided to allow them

residual_themes.theme_label: Avoidance of inflammatory, trolling, or disrespectful language/intent
residual_themes.definition: A recurring residual idea is to reject content when it is seen as inflammatory, crude, abusive, hateful/bad-language, a rant, or trolling—because it undermines productive discussion/healthy debate or signals low informational value.

example.feature_value: Tried to ignore political content and interpret content as venting vs argumentative.
example.evidence_span: I tried to ignore the political content. I looked for swearing and words that weren't about making an argument, but about venting anger.

residual_themes.definition: Decisions hinge on whether statements are fact-based, verifiable, accurate, or not provably false/misinformation. Falsehoods or harmful misinformation trigger removal even when other factors (e.g., free-speech framing) might otherwise support inclusion.

example.feature_value: Keep opinions; remove if nonsense/lies with harmful effects
example.evidence_span: If it was something that was mainly an opinion, I thought it should stay... If it appeared to be nonsense... and I thought it was actually harmful, I thought it should be removed... But if they are flat out lies, I think they should not remain.

residual_themes.theme_label: Healthy debate / discussion-conduciveness as the selection criterion
residual_themes.definition: A set of residual items focuses on whether content supports healthy political dialogue—e.g., encourages discussion/engagement, offers constructive debate/value, and remains within a conversational boundary. Uncertainty often leads to not removing/allowing rules aligned with discussion goals.

example.feature_value: Not fully consistent; later realized some allowed content wasn’t conducive to healthy political dialogue.
example.evidence_span: I'm not sure I was entirely consistent... Some of what I allowed was not conducive to healthy political dialogue.

residual_themes.definition: Several features reflect residual process constraints where the interface or the decision logic forces pair-level treatment—either both are kept/removed, both are considered together as a unit, or reciprocal/symmetric mirroring is required.

example.feature_value: Preferred leaving posts up to provide full perspectives, noting emotionally charged claims without evidence but constraints on removing only one.
example.evidence_span: People deserve to have all perspective's laid out before them even if we don't trust them to be able to decipher reason from hysteria.
